slot.brief: Rank acidity of terminal alkyne vs alkene vs alkane, or identify which alkynyl anion forms with NaNH2; conceptual comparison with reagent recognition.

stem: Arrange these compounds in decreasing order of acidity: ethyne, ethene and ethane.

verdicts.working: Acidity increases as pKa decreases: ethyne (pKa ≈ 25) > ethene (≈ 44) > ethane (≈ 50).

working:
Greater $s$-character stabilises the conjugate base: $sp > sp^2 > sp^3$.\nThus acidity: ethyne $>$ ethene $>$ ethane.

Independent check: Acidity increases as pKa decreases: ethyne (pKa ≈ 25) > ethene (≈ 44) > ethane (≈ 50).
solution:
Greater $s$-character stabilises the conjugate base: $sp > sp^2 > sp^3$.
Thus, the acidity order is ethyne $>$ ethene $>$ ethane, giving (C).
